newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japanese oil dealer, two former execs arrested.
newsitem.headline: Japanese oil dealer, two former execs arrested.

text.p: A Japanese oil wholesaler, arrested last year on massive tax evasion charges, was arrested again on fraud charges on Wednesday along with two former oil company exutives, police said.

Osaka oil dealer Junichi Izui, whose close ties to trade ministry officials embarrassed the ministry last year, was served with a fresh arrest warrant in connection with a 2.39 billion yen ($20.6 million) fraud, Tokyo prosecutors said.

Also arrested on suspicion of fraud were Takeshi Otsuki, former deputy chief of Mitsubishi Oil Co's Tokyo branch, and Masanori Kozuma, former deputy director of Mitsui Mining, the Tokyo District Public Prosecutor's office said.
Mistui Mining is natural resource firm which derives 25 percent of its revenue from petroleum.
Prosecutors said the fraud at Mitsui Mining occurred between May and August 1995.
Izui, owner of an Osaka-based oil firm, was arrested in November on suspicion of evading 330 million yen in income tax on oil deal commissions between 1992 and 1994.
The arrest of Izui prompted a ministry survey which revealed that more than 100 bureaucrats had dined, drank or golfed with him. Several senior bureaucrats were disciplined over the case.
